title: stitching-session-brief-kiara-2026-03-22
content:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for a short (45m) cross-functional sync to stitch product priorities with engineering capacity and applied-ML experiments. Goal is to leave with: 1) a prioritized rollout plan for Q2 features that balances latency/cost tradeoffs, 2) a small set of concrete experiments (MVP) for model quantization and routing policy, and 3) clear owners + deadlines for follow-ups.

Logistics:
- Meeting length: 45 minutes (standup style). Proposed time: Tue 2026-03-24 10:00-10:45 PT.
- Attendees (requested): Emma Chen (PM, Product), Rajiv Kumar (Eng lead, Serving Runtime), Nora Li (Applied ML), Miguel Torres (SRE), me (Kiara) as convener.
- Pre-reads: short bullets in Confluence (linked), experimental results summary from Nora (embeddings perf vs quant), Rajiv's capacity note (attached comment in PR). Ask people to skim before.

Agenda (tight):
1) Quick frame (3m) — why this sync now (Q2 milestone: low-latency gen for search, cost target -20%).
2) Surface risks / constraints (7m) — infra capacity, holiday infra changes, telemetry gaps.
3) Product priorities & tradeoffs (10m) — Emma: top 3 customer-facing features and must-have SLOs.
4) Eng constraints & options (10m) — Rajiv: Dedicated pools vs shared-hosted fallback; autoscale windows; quantization ops.
5) Research experiments (8m) — Nora: proposed 3-step experiments for 8-bit/4-bit and KV-cache changes, success metrics.
6) Decisions & Next actions (7m) — owners, deadlines, and immediate blockers.

Key prep notes / talking points to raise:
- Product wants GenSearch feature (beam reranking + streaming snippets). Primary SLO: 95th percentile latency under 450ms for snippets in hosted mode. Cost objective: <0.008 $/token equivalent for query pipeline.
- Eng: serving runtime can meet latency if we reserve a Dedicated pool for daytime peak (09:00-18:00 PT) but cost increases ~1.7x. Need to decide whether to accept higher commit for Q2 MVP or mitigate via aggressive caching/batching.
- Applied ML: quantization to 4-bit (GPT-small equivalent) reduces GPU memory footprint enabling denser packing, but early evals show a 2–3% regression on snippet relevance (NDCG). Propose canary: route 10% of low-risk traffic to quantized variant with automated rollback on quality delta >1.5%.
- Fallback strategy: if Dedicated pool saturates, automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant with degraded token generation length (max tokens reduced) vs synchronous queue. Which fallback triggers first? engineering preference: region-then-variant fallback. Product preference: preserve UX (streaming) at cost of lower length. Need alignment.

Metrics / success criteria to agree on in meeting:
- Latency SLO: p95 < 450ms for snippet streaming; p99 < 1s (for core path).
- Quality guardrail: NDCG drop < 1.5% for production changes vs baseline on held-out prompt set.
- Cost goal: end-to-end token-equivalent cost per query < target (PM to provide target bucket).
- Rollout guard: automated quality checks and rollback within 30 minutes of anomaly detection.

Open questions (parked):
- Can SRE temporarily increase quota on Dedicated GPUs for two weeks to accelerate rollout? (Miguel)
- Does legal/security need to review the routing policy for cross-region fallbacks? (check with Security)
- Is there appetite to accept a slightly higher downstream latency for rare long snippets in exchange for 25% cost reduction? (Product decision)

Concrete experiments Nora proposes (short summary):
- Exp A (week 1): 8-bit quantization + cache hot-prefix preservation. Traffic policy: 5% random. Metrics: NDCG, p95 latency, mem usage.
- Exp B (week 2–3): 4-bit (Q4) quant + low-temp decoding for rerank path. Traffic: 10% canary on low-value customer cohort. Auto-rollback if NDCG delta >1.5%.
- Exp C (parallel): routing policy test — route to Dedicated when estimated token-cost > threshold OR when user tier == enterprise; else host on cheaper variant. Measure shard imbalance and CPU/GPU utilization.

Tradeoffs for meeting to surface quickly:
- Reserve Dedicated (higher commit) vs rely on smarter routing + cache (lower commit, more complex ops).
- Aggressive quantization (cost down, small quality hit) vs slower rollout with more manual evals (higher cost).
- Region-first fallback vs variant-first fallback (latency vs privacy/compliance).

Draft decisions I want us to land on in this sync:
- Approve a small Dedicated commitment for core roadmap hours (09:00-18:00 PT) for Q2 MVP with a documented rollback point.
- Approve Exp A and Exp B run schedule with Nora and assign telemetry owner.
- Standardize fallback order: region->variant->queue, but allow product-override for flagged flows.

Action items (explicit) — use as follow-ups after meeting:
- Kiara: update Confluence with final plan + timeline; sync with finance for cost delta estimate. Due: 2026-03-27.
- Emma: provide precise cost target bucket and customer cohorts (prod vs low-value) to route. Due: 2026-03-25.
- Rajiv: draft Dedicated commit proposal (GPU count, hours, autoscale policy) and infra PR. Attach capacity runbook. Due: 2026-03-26.
- Nora: upload baseline eval scripts and initial 8-bit/4-bit artifact with notes on NDCG delta; define automated check thresholds. Due: 2026-03-26.
- Miguel: confirm quota increase possibility and side-effects; add SRE runbook for emergency rollback. Due: 2026-03-25.
- All: quick thumbs-up thread in Slack once pre-reads done (tag @channel). Due: before meeting.

Notes-to-self & prep reminders:
- Bring plain-language explanation of fallback options (one slide).
- Have a small table showing cost delta per 100k queries for Dedicated vs hosted with/without quantization.
- Be ready to propose an immediate alpha rollout (only internal users) if we can get SRE quota.
- Keep the meeting focused: avoid deep dive on model training — we only need inference/eval outcomes here.

Parking lot (if time remains):
- Longer-term: evaluate kernel-selection heuristics per model family to optimize p95 for long-context queries.
- Post-mvp: product asks for telemetry surfacing in Console (token-level cost for route variant). Put on roadmap for Optimize team.

Rough timeline (post-meeting):
- Week 1: approvals + Dedicated commit PR + baseline experiment A start.
- Week 2: monitoring & experiment B schedule.
- Week 3–4: evaluate, roll canary to low-value cohort, decide full rollout.

Quick reference links (again):
- Confluence: RDW-ROADMAP-2026 (linked_artifacts).
- RFC: kernel-selection and batching PR (#412).
- JIRA: INF-2345 (Dedicated commit), RDW-987 (quant experiments).

Finish: This is intentionally a compact prep doc — lots of rough bullets. Keep it flexible during the sync. After meeting copy final notes + decisions into Confluence and create a JIRA epic for the Q2 rollout if we greenlight.

-- Kiara
